correctness.rationale: The reflection involution turns the second Cauchy--Schwarz term into the negative-shift autocorrelation, giving coefficientwise improvement and an exact determinant-square difference. L2 is invariant. RMS balancing strictly increases the coefficient sum unless magnitudes are symmetric, so some nonzero autocorrelation increases. Each even moment has a nonnegative sum over zero-total lag tuples; the pair (h,-h) forces simultaneous strictness for every s>=2. Compactness yields necessary symmetry of all maximizers. Verification code tests cyclic exact integer examples and phases without replacing the infinite general proof.

originality.rationale: The principal new content is simultaneous *lagwise* autocorrelation majorization by RMS reflection for arbitrary finite supports in discrete abelian groups, including a strict equality criterion and necessary symmetry for every even-exponent maximizer. The classical Hardy--Littlewood majorant addresses phase deletion, not balancing mirror magnitudes; the palindrome-equicorrelation literature addresses preservation, not monotone growth. Searches and inspected primary texts did not show a dominating implication; historical symmetrization terminology remains a material residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent elementary reflection-balancing lemma may occur under traditional rearrangement/symmetrization nomenclature outside the inspected literature.
Goldstein--McDonald (1984) An Extremal Problem for Non-Negative Trigonometric Polynomials was found bibliographically; its full text was not obtained and no noncoverage inference is made.
The theorem does not establish sharp numerical constants or phase-classification statements for arbitrary finite supports.

value.rationale: The universal lagwise inequality simultaneously solves a natural reduction issue for all even Fourier norm extremization problems with centered symmetric frequency support, for any finite length and any discrete abelian group. It proves that *every* norm maximizer has reflection-invariant magnitudes (not merely that one symmetric example exists), with an explicit determinant-square defect. This is an infinite structural statement beyond any fixed small-frequency computation. It does not claim a downstream sharp norm; value lies in the constructive dimension reduction and exact equality criterion.
